issues.legal_issue: The relationship of eyewitnesses to the deceased and their questionable antecedents do not justify rejecting their testimony wholesale.
material_facts: The eyewitnesses were related to the deceased and had questionable antecedents.
They lived with the deceased in the same hamlet, and their presence with him at the time and place of the occurrence was probable.
The appellate court rejected their evidence wholesale instead of assessing the role attributed to each accused.
issues.conclusion: The witnesses’ relationship to the deceased and their antecedents were not valid grounds, by themselves, for rejecting their evidence; their testimony required careful scrutiny, with credible parts accepted and unreliable parts rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Related or interested witnesses and witnesses with questionable antecedents are not necessarily untruthful. Their evidence must be examined with more than ordinary care and circumspection, including by considering the role attributed to each accused and whether surrounding circumstances provide assurance. No earlier case was cited for this principle.

predicates.criminal_trial: The proceeding is a criminal trial in which the prosecution relies on eyewitness testimony.
predicates.eyewitnesses_related: The eyewitnesses are related to the deceased.
predicates.witnesses_have_questionable_antecedents: The eyewitnesses have antecedents of a questionable nature.

issues.definition: When a criminal trial relies on related eyewitnesses with questionable antecedents, their testimony requires careful scrutiny rather than automatic rejection.

issues.legal_issue: Discrepancies about collateral details do not justify rejecting eyewitness testimony when the core account is consistent.
material_facts: The witnesses differed about whether they and the deceased had left their hamlet on the day of the occurrence or a day earlier.
The witnesses testified about the events approximately seventeen months after the occurrence.
Their evidence was consistent on the substance of the prosecution account, and the defence had not cross-examined one witness about his whereabouts on the previous night.
issues.conclusion: The discrepancies about collateral details did not justify concluding that the witnesses were absent from the scene or rejecting their testimony.
issues.legal_principle: Discrepancies about subsidiary facts or matters of detail may occur even in truthful testimony, particularly after a substantial passage of time. They are not ordinarily a ground for rejecting evidence when the witnesses generally agree about the substratum of the case.

predicates.criminal_trial: The proceeding is a criminal trial in which the prosecution relies on eyewitness testimony.
predicates.discrepancies_are_collateral: The witnesses differ about subsidiary details rather than the substance of the alleged occurrence.
predicates.core_account_is_consistent: The witnesses generally agree about the central events of the prosecution case.

issues.definition: In a criminal trial, collateral discrepancies do not justify rejecting eyewitness testimony when the core account remains consistent.

issues.legal_issue: A promptly lodged first information report can provide valuable corroboration of the informant’s testimony.
material_facts: The informant testified that the occurrence took place at about 3:30 p.m. and that he reported it at the police station at 4:30 p.m.
The police station was about three miles from the bus stand where the informant said he retrieved his motorcycle.
A copy of the report reached a magistrate that same evening, and medical evidence supported the informant’s account of the time of death.
The report contained material facts, including the names of the accused and witnesses.
issues.conclusion: The prompt report, made without undue delay and with little opportunity to concoct a false story, furnished valuable corroboration of the informant’s trial testimony.
issues.legal_principle: The court treated the promptness and contents of the first information report, recorded under Section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as circumstances providing valuable corroboration of the informant’s testimony. No earlier case was cited for this application.

predicates.criminal_prosecution: The proceeding is a criminal prosecution in which the informant gives evidence about the alleged offence.
predicates.informant_makes_report_promptly: The informant reports the occurrence soon after it happens, with little opportunity to fabricate an account.
predicates.report_contains_material_details: The report records material details of the alleged occurrence, including relevant identities or events.

issues.definition: In a criminal prosecution, a prompt report containing material details corroborates the informant’s testimony.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to use independent local witnesses for a recovery may reduce the recovery evidence’s weight but does not make it inadmissible.
material_facts: An accused made a statement leading to the discovery of a rifle and cartridges.
The investigating officer relied on police personnel rather than independent local persons or community members to witness the statement and recovery.
The recovery evidence was supported by testimony, and an expert linked a cartridge recovered at the scene to the rifle.
issues.conclusion: The omission of independent local witnesses devalued the recovery evidence but did not render it inadmissible or, by itself, justify excluding it altogether.
issues.legal_principle: The absence of independent witnesses to a recovery affects the weight of that evidence but does not make it inadmissible. In this case, the investigating officer’s demonstrated partiality toward the defence also made fabrication of the recovery on behalf of the prosecution less likely.

predicates.criminal_investigation: The proceeding involves a criminal investigation and evidence gathered during it.
predicates.accused_leads_to_discovery: An accused makes information that leads investigators to discover an item relevant to the alleged offence.
predicates.investigator_omits_independent_recovery_: The investigator does not have independent local persons witness the statement or resulting recovery.

issues.definition: When an accused leads investigators to a relevant discovery but the investigator does not use independent recovery witnesses, the recovery evidence remains admissible but carries reduced weight.

issues.legal_issue: An acquittal may be set aside on a State appeal where eyewitness testimony against an accused receives sufficient assurance from prompt reporting and other evidence.
material_facts: The State appealed from an acquittal in a murder prosecution.
Two eyewitnesses consistently identified two accused as participating in the killing of one deceased.
The informant’s prompt report supported the eyewitness account.
Evidence of motive supported one accused, while motive and the recovery of a rifle linked by expert evidence to a cartridge at the scene provided further assurance against the other.
issues.conclusion: The acquittal of the two accused was set aside, and they were convicted of the murder of the deceased under Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues.legal_principle: In assessing interested eyewitness testimony, the court required assurance from surrounding circumstances or other evidence as a matter of caution. It found that the prompt report, evidence of motive, and the firearm evidence sufficiently supported the testimony against these accused. The court applied Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and cited no earlier cases for this conclusion.

predicates.state_appeal_from_acquittal: The State appeals against the acquittal of persons accused of a criminal offence.
predicates.eyewitnesses_identify_accused: Eyewitnesses identify the accused as participating in the alleged homicide.
predicates.testimony_has_corroborative_assurance: The eyewitness testimony is supported by surrounding circumstances or other evidence, such as a prompt report, motive, or forensic evidence.

issues.definition: On a State appeal from an acquittal, identified accused may be convicted for the homicide when eyewitness testimony has corroborative assurance.

issues.legal_issue: An acquittal should be maintained where the evidence against an accused lacks sufficient assurance of participation in the homicide.
material_facts: The evidence did not establish that the remaining accused had a motive to kill either deceased.
One accused was found nearby shortly after the killings while engaged in ordinary agricultural activity.
The eyewitnesses began fleeing after the first deceased was shot and could have had only a fleeting view of the later events and assailants.
The eyewitness evidence against these accused lacked the corroborative assurance found for the two accused whose acquittals were set aside.
issues.conclusion: The remaining accused received the benefit of doubt, and their acquittals on all counts were maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the evidence against each accused separately. Where eyewitness evidence lacked sufficient assurance, and the circumstances left a reasonable doubt about participation, the accused received the benefit of doubt. No earlier case was cited for this application.

rule.if: state_appeal_from_acquittal and evidence_lacks_accused_specific_assurance and (no_established_motive or observation_was_fleeting)

predicates.state_appeal_from_acquittal: The State appeals against the acquittal of persons accused of a criminal offence.
predicates.evidence_lacks_accused_specific_assuranc: The evidence against an accused lacks supporting circumstances that reliably connect that accused to the alleged homicide.
predicates.no_established_motive: The prosecution does not establish a motive for the accused to commit the alleged homicide.
predicates.observation_was_fleeting: The witnesses had only a brief or distant opportunity to observe the accused’s alleged participation.

issues.definition: On a State appeal from an acquittal, an accused receives the benefit of doubt and remains acquitted when the evidence lacks accused-specific assurance and either no motive is established or the observation was fleeting.
